Here are 10 well-known open-source vector databases. This comes from my own knowledge, not a live check, so confirm licenses against each repo before relying on them, since projects sometimes relicense.

| # | Name | GitHub URL | License | Language |
|---|------|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Milvus | https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus | Apache-2.0 | Go (with C++ core) |
| 2 | Qdrant | https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant | Apache-2.0 | Rust |
| 3 | Weaviate | https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate | BSD-3-Clause | Go |
| 4 | Chroma | https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma | Apache-2.0 | Rust (originally Python) |
| 5 | pgvector | https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector | PostgreSQL License | C |
| 6 | Faiss | https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss | MIT | C++ |
| 7 | LanceDB | https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb | Apache-2.0 | Rust |
| 8 | Vespa | https://github.com/vespa-engine/vespa | Apache-2.0 | Java and C++ |
| 9 | Annoy | https://github.com/spotify/annoy | Apache-2.0 | C++ (with Python bindings) |
| 10 | Vald | https://github.com/vdaas/vald | Apache-2.0 | Go |

- **Faiss and Annoy** are libraries for similarity search, not full database servers. They're often grouped with vector databases, though.
- **pgvector** is a PostgreSQL extension, not a standalone database.
- **Chroma** moved its core to Rust, but the project still ships a lot of Python.
- **Other candidates:** Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (k-NN) and Redis (vector search) are also used for vectors. Their licenses have changed over time, so I left them out. I can swap any of the 10 above for them if you like.

I can also check the current license and primary language of each repo through the GitHub API, if you'd like that.
